clue.text: Political group substitutes seat of government

parts.note: a front is a political movement, as in the National Front
in sport the substitutes sit on the bench

explanation.surface: A party is replacing the official home of the administration.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons the front benches are where ministers (and their shadows) sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministers of the governing party sit on the front bench in Parliament, so it is literally where government sits.

clue.text: Jack and Iris become tired

definitions.meaning: a jack is a ship's ..., as in the Union Jack
the yellow iris is commonly called a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a kind of banner, the flag is a wild iris, and to flag is to tire.

clue.text: Bishop taken in by old maid perhaps following religion

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held within it, so the bishop's letter sits inside

parts.note: a maid is one example of a servant
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is employed by an elderly housemaid who is devout.
explanation.definitionFit: An observant believer is one who keeps the rules and practices of their faith.

clue.text: Leading light in Fleet Street drank

parts.note: top means leading or foremost
an editor, ED, is a leading figure on a newspaper; Fleet Street was London's newspaper district

explanation.surface: A star journalist went drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading light' reads as one phrase meaning a star, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is an old word for drinking alcohol heavily, so the past tense means drank.

clue.text: European behind such as Chinese

parts.note: astern means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A European following someone such as a Chinese person.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese is an example of something from the Orient, described as of the East.

clue.text: Talk about person said to be mad

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
the saying is 'mad as a hatter'

explanation.surface: Discussing someone who is reputedly insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter is idle, rapid talk, so the two are synonyms as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Sounds like robust greeting

indicators.note: says the word for robust is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: hale means healthy and robust

explanation.surface: A hearty welcome is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A hail is a call of greeting, as in 'hail, friend'.

clue.text: Clay when getting another name

parts.note: Cassius Clay was the boxer Muhammad Ali's birth name
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Cassius Clay at the time he took a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Clay himself took another name, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed second name someone goes by.

clue.text: Fruit began to be arranged in transporter

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a lorry is a British truck that transports goods

indicators.note: the letters of began are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Fruit started to be packed into a goods vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A loganberry is a hybrid berry, a cross between raspberry and blackberry.

clue.text: In terrible heat I work on island in African country

indicators.note: the work and island letters are placed inside the anagram
terrible signals that heat and I are jumbled

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone toils on an island in fierce heat in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a nation in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: A set backing fabulous author

indicators.note: backing means the word for set is read backwards

parts.note: to pose a question is to set it

explanation.surface: A collection returning to a famous writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' here means writing fables, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop wrote fables, so he is literally a fabulous, fable-writing, author.

clue.text: Amazing bird seen round top of tree

indicators.note: the bird's name goes round the extra letter

parts.note: a starling is a common songbird

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of tree

explanation.surface: A remarkable bird spotted circling a treetop.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means surprising or astonishing, the same as amazing.

clue.text: One's inclined to allow end to be held

indicators.note: the word for end is held inside the word for allow

parts.note: to grant is to allow
to die is to end

explanation.surface: Someone leaning towards letting the end be contained.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, something that is inclined.

clue.text: Playwright's digestive problem requiring nurse

parts.note: IBS is irritable bowel syndrome
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A dramatist's stomach trouble needs a nurse's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House.

clue.text: Half accept phone signal cut off in Stanley's place

indicators.note: half takes the first three letters of accept
cut off removes the last letter

parts.note: a ringtone is a phone's call signal

explanation.surface: A phone signal drops halfway through accepting a call from Stanley.
explanation.walkthrough: Accrington Stanley is a football club from the Lancashire town of Accrington. 'cut off' drops the final E of RINGTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The town gives its name to the football club Accrington Stanley, so it is Stanley's home.

clue.text: Conservative needs to make rapid progress in discipline

parts.note: to hasten is to hurry along

explanation.surface: A Tory must speed up in matters of discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to correct or punish, a synonym of the verb discipline.

clue.text: What business makes pie?

definitions.meaning: the total sales a business makes in a period
a pastry folded over a filling

explanation.definitionFit: Turnover is both a company's sales total and a folded pastry such as an apple turnover.

clue.text: Unconventional priest's locked up over sharp reply

indicators.note: the priest letters hold the extra letter inside
the letters of priest are put in an unusual order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: An odd clergyman has been jailed for a cutting retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconventional' turns PRIEST into RIPSTE, which takes O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, witty retort, originally a fencing counterthrust.

clue.text: Prove a sun explodes — as this?

definitions.text: Prove a sun explodes — as this?

indicators.note: explodes signals that the letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Does a star demonstrate it is exploding?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: a star blowing apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is the explosion of a star, so an exploding sun is one.

clue.text: One no longer working on Hebridean island

parts.note: re means on, concerning
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A pensioner living on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiree has stopped work, usually on reaching pension age.

clue.text: Hot former lover called

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
cited means summoned, called to court

explanation.surface: An old flame phoned and the conversation was heated.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot can mean aroused or worked up, as excited does.

clue.text: A paper round with right paper wrongly delivered

indicators.note: letters delivered wrongly arrive in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A newspaper round where the right paper went to the wrong house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A paper round' reads as a delivery job, but it is the definition: paper wrapped round something. 'wrongly delivered' turns W, R and PAPER into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is a covering of paper folded around something such as a sweet.

clue.text: Walter's profligate good-for-nothing

indicators.note: profligate means wildly wasteful, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Walter is a spendthrift and a layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is a wasteful idler, a worthless person.

clue.text: In Spain a chorizo is a spicy snack

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the run of words

explanation.surface: In Spain, chorizo sausage is a spicy nibble.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip topped with cheese and chilli.

clue.text: Load carried initially by legendary ship

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of carried

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Freight carried by the mythical ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods loaded on a ship or plane.

clue.text: Money gets nothing more than fine material

parts.note: cash is money
mere means nothing more than, as in 'a mere child'

explanation.surface: Cash buys only good cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a soft, fine wool from Kashmir goats.

clue.text: Small child swallows slice of roast joint

indicators.note: the child word takes the extra letter inside it

parts.note: a mite is a small child

indicators.note: a slice of roast here is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A toddler eats a piece of roast beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a corner joint in woodwork where two angled ends meet.

clue.text: Bet TV presenter takes drug

parts.note: Ant McPartlin is half of the British TV duo Ant and Dec
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A gamble that a TV host is taking narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put into the pot in poker.

clue.text: Half of our race between two peaks is cause of suffering

indicators.note: the half goes between the two hill words

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill peak, as on Dartmoor
the second tor of the pair
men are half the human race

explanation.surface: Half of humanity racing between two summits is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our race' is the human race, half of whom are MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is someone who causes another distress or pain.

clue.text: Spike Milligan's final letter revealed by the 'Thunderer'

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

indicators.note: takes only the last letter of Milligan

explanation.surface: Spike Milligan's last letter appears in The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like comedian Spike Milligan's first name, but it is the definition; the Thunderer is also a nickname for The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant stem.

clue.text: Retreat lacking approval?

parts.note: no means lacking, as in 'no money'
OK is approval

explanation.surface: Withdrawal without the go-ahead?
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a secluded spot, a quiet retreat.

clue.text: Debase worship around Troy's first queen

indicators.note: the worship word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to adulate is to worship or flatter

indicators.note: takes the first letter of Troy

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Degrade the adoration surrounding Troy's first queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to make something impure, lowering its quality.
